features.title: pytest Infrastructure and Shared Conftest Fixtures
features.description:
This module creates the entire pytest dev infrastructure for the brownfield project: a
`requirements-dev.txt` at the project root with `pytest>=8` and `pytest-asyncio`, an empty
`tests/__init__.py` package marker, and a `tests/conftest.py` that provides the shared fixtures
consumed by every downstream test module.

The project context is a two-agent Python CLI application described in
`.aah/architecture/architecture-overview.md` (§Layer Summary, §Technology Decisions). The two
agents — `agentic_app.py` (synchronous filesystem/shell coding assistant) and `agentic_tester.py`
(async Playwright browser QA agent) — both call the Anthropic SDK and, in the tester's case, drive
a real Chromium process. The testing landscape and coupling risks are documented in
`.aah/codebase-intel/codebase-learning.md` (§9 Testing Landscape, §11 Technical Debt). The module
only scaffolds the dev infrastructure; it does not write any test assertions — those belong to
MOD-002 as recorded in `.aah/architecture/module-map.yaml`.

**Stack:** Python 3.12, pytest>=8, pytest-asyncio, `unittest.mock` (stdlib). No model calls and no
browser process are started during the test run; both are replaced by mock fixtures so the suite
runs fully offline.

**conftest.py fixtures to implement:**

1. `mock_anthropic_client` (function-scoped) — a `unittest.mock.MagicMock` (or `AsyncMock` for
   async paths) that replicates the `anthropic.Anthropic` / `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` client
   interface. Its `messages.create` (and `messages.acreate`) return a controlled response object
   whose `stop_reason` is `"tool_use"` on the first call and `"end_turn"` on the second, with a
   `content` list carrying a `tool_use` block containing a predictable `name` and `input` dict.
   This allows tests for `execute_tool` and `_run_tool` to exercise the full dispatch path without
   any network call.

2. `mock_page` (function-scoped, `pytest.mark.asyncio` compatible) — an `AsyncMock` that replicates
   the `playwright.async_api.Page` interface. At minimum it must expose `goto`, `click`,
   `fill`, `evaluate`, and `query_selector` as async stubs returning sensible defaults so that
   browser-tool unit tests in `tests/test_run_tool.py` can call `_run_tool` with predictable
   outcomes.

Both fixtures must be defined at the top of `tests/conftest.py` with standard pytest `@pytest.fixture`
decorators. `pytest-asyncio` must be configured for `asyncio_mode = "auto"` (via a `pytest.ini_options`
section in `pyproject.toml` or a `[pytest]` section in `pytest.ini`, or as a `conftest.py`-level
`pytest_configure` hook) so that async test functions in MOD-002 do not require per-test
`@pytest.mark.asyncio` decoration.

**Behavioral expectations:**

- Given `requirements-dev.txt` is created at the project root with `pytest>=8` and
  `pytest-asyncio`, when a developer runs `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`, then the command
  exits 0, both `pytest` and `pytest_asyncio` are importable, and no package listed conflicts with
  the production `requirements.txt` (`anthropic>=1.0.0`, `playwright>=1.40.0`).
- Given the `tests/` package exists with `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/conftest.py`, when
  `pytest --collect-only` is run from the project root, then the command exits 0 with no collection
  errors (the package is discoverable and no syntax errors are present in conftest).
- Given `tests/conftest.py` exports the `mock_anthropic_client` fixture, when a test function
  requests it, then it receives a mock whose `messages.create` returns an object with
  `stop_reason = "tool_use"` on the first call and `stop_reason = "end_turn"` on the second, and no
  HTTP connection to `api.anthropic.com` is opened during the test.
- Given `tests/conftest.py` exports the `mock_page` fixture, when an async test function requests
  it, then it receives an `AsyncMock` Page object whose awaitable methods (`goto`, `click`, `fill`,
  `evaluate`, `query_selector`) resolve without error and no Chromium browser process is spawned.
- Given `pytest-asyncio` is configured with `asyncio_mode = "auto"`, when an `async def test_*`
  function in the `tests/` package runs, then it completes without the
  `PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` or `no event loop` errors that arise from missing asyncio
  mode configuration.
- Given `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is the runtime secret required by both agents (see
  `.aah/architecture/architecture-overview.md` §Technology Decisions and
  `.aah/codebase-intel/codebase-learning.md` §10 Build and Deployment), when the project's
  `.env.example` file is inspected, then `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` appears as a named entry with a safe
  placeholder value (e.g. `your-api-key-here`), confirming the variable is documented for
  developers who clone the repo.
- Given the conftest fixtures mock the Anthropic client and Playwright page, when the full test
  suite (`pytest tests/ -v`) is run without a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in the environment,
  then all tests that use only these fixtures still pass — the mock layer must fully isolate the
  suite from the live API and browser.

features.title: Capability-Scoped Auth Gate for Agent Tools
features.description:
MOD-001 is a purely additive security-hardening patch to two existing Python CLI agents. It annotates
all 11 tool calls with a `CAPABILITY_MAP` constant, inserts a pre-dispatch capability check inside
both `execute_tool()` (`agentic_app.py:142`) and `_run_tool()` (`agentic_tester.py:150`), introduces
a `CapabilityError` custom exception raised on blocked calls, and adds `MAX_ITERATIONS = 20` to
`agentic_tester.py` to match the main agent's pre-existing iteration cap. The stack is Python 3.12
with the `anthropic` SDK; no new third-party dependencies are introduced. Changes are confined to
`agentic_app.py` and `agentic_tester.py` as additive patches — no rewrite.

Refer to these architecture sources for normative detail:

- `.aah/architecture/agent-topology.md` — Agent Profiles (executor entry points, loop style,
  iteration cap) and Capability Map table (the definitive tool-to-capability mapping for all 11 tools).
- `.aah/architecture/data-model.md` — `CAPABILITY_MAP` and `CapabilityError` data structure
  definitions; capability check data-flow diagram showing how `CapabilityError` feeds back into the
  `tool_result` path.
- `.aah/architecture/application-flow.md` — Tool-Calling Loop with Capability Validation sequence
  diagram; happy-path, blocked-path, and iteration-cap-path variants; QA Agent Differences table.
- `.aah/architecture/architecture-overview.md` — Security Controls layer, full Architecture Diagram,
  and Constraints section (explicitly deferred items: `run_command` safelist, `check_env()` wiring,
  `REQUIRED_ENV` hardening, browser state isolation).

The 5 main-agent tools and their capability strings (from `.aah/architecture/agent-topology.md`
Capability Map table): `read_file → ["filesystem.read"]`, `list_files → ["filesystem.read"]`,
`run_command → ["shell.exec"]`, `write_file → ["filesystem.write"]`,
`search_in_file → ["filesystem.read"]`.

The 6 QA-agent tools and their capability strings: `open_page → ["browser.navigate"]`,
`click_button → ["browser.interact"]`, `fill_and_submit → ["browser.interact", "browser.submit"]`,
`resize_viewport → ["browser.viewport"]`, `get_computed_style → ["browser.read"]`,
`record_result → ["memory.write"]`.

**Behavioral expectations:**

- Given `agentic_app` is imported, when `CAPABILITY_MAP` is accessed at module level, then it is a
  `dict[str, list[str]]` with exactly 5 entries — `read_file`, `list_files`, `run_command`,
  `write_file`, `search_in_file` — each mapped to the capability strings shown in the Capability Map
  table of `.aah/architecture/agent-topology.md`; `len(CAPABILITY_MAP) == 5` is true.
- Given `agentic_tester` is imported, when `CAPABILITY_MAP` is accessed at module level, then it is a
  `dict[str, list[str]]` with exactly 6 entries — `open_page`, `click_button`, `fill_and_submit`,
  `resize_viewport`, `get_computed_style`, `record_result` — each mapped to the capability strings
  shown in the Capability Map table of `.aah/architecture/agent-topology.md`; `len(CAPABILITY_MAP) == 6`
  is true.
- Given `agentic_tester` is imported, when `MAX_ITERATIONS` is accessed at module level, then
  `MAX_ITERATIONS == 20` is true, matching the main agent's pre-existing cap per the QA Agent
  Differences table in `.aah/architecture/application-flow.md`.
- Given `execute_tool` is called with a tool name whose `CAPABILITY_MAP` entry covers the requested
  operation, when the pre-dispatch capability check passes, then the existing tool implementation
  executes and returns the same result string as the pre-patch code — no behavior regression for
  allowed calls.
- Given `execute_tool` is called with a tool name whose `CAPABILITY_MAP` entry does not cover the
  requested operation (e.g. `write_file` with `filesystem.write` blocked), when the pre-dispatch
  check fails, then `CapabilityError` is raised before the tool implementation runs and before any
  filesystem or subprocess action occurs.
- Given `_run_tool` is called (async) with a tool name whose `CAPABILITY_MAP` entry covers the
  requested operation, when the pre-dispatch capability check passes, then the existing async browser
  tool implementation executes and returns the same JSON-encoded result string as the pre-patch code.
- Given `_run_tool` is called (async) with a tool name whose `CAPABILITY_MAP` entry does not cover
  the requested operation (e.g. `open_page` with `browser.navigate` blocked), when the pre-dispatch
  check fails, then `CapabilityError` is raised before the browser implementation runs.
- Given `CapabilityError` is instantiated with a message string, when it is raised and caught, then
  it is a subclass of `Exception`, and both `str(err)` and `err.args[0]` return the original
  message; the calling agent loop can use that message as `tool_result` content so the loop continues
  without crashing, as described in the blocked-path flow in `.aah/architecture/application-flow.md`.
- Given `agentic_tester.py`'s async `run` loop, when the iteration counter reaches `MAX_ITERATIONS`
  (20) before `stop_reason == "end_turn"`, then the while loop exits cleanly, `_results` are printed
  to stdout, and no unhandled exception is raised — mirroring the iteration-cap path described in
  `.aah/architecture/application-flow.md`.
- Given all 5 tools in `agentic_app.py` are called through `execute_tool` with inputs that pass the
  capability check, when each runs against its pre-existing implementation, then each returns the same
  result as the pre-patch code; the capability-auth patch introduces no behavior regression on the
  allowed path.
- Given all 6 browser tools in `agentic_tester.py` are called through `_run_tool` (async) with
  inputs that pass the capability check, when each runs against its pre-existing implementation, then
  each returns the same JSON-encoded result as the pre-patch code; no behavior regression on the
  allowed path.
- Given the project is configured for first use, when `.env.example` is inspected, then it contains
  an entry for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with a placeholder value (the `check_env()` startup wiring is
  explicitly deferred per `.aah/architecture/architecture-overview.md` Constraints and is not in
  scope for this module).

features.title: pytest Test Suite and Golden Evals
features.description:
This module creates the automated test suite for the security controls introduced in MOD-001, as described in `architecture-overview.md` (Test Suite layer) and grounded in user story 2 and 4 from `discuss/discuss-prd.md`. It produces four pytest test files and one golden evaluation YAML file, all under a new `tests/` tree built on the scaffold established by MOD-000. No model calls are needed to run the suite — the Anthropic client is replaced by the mock fixture in `tests/conftest.py`.

The five artefacts and their responsibilities:

**`tests/test_execute_tool.py`** — unit tests for `execute_tool()` in `agentic_app.py` (see lines 142–218 as profiled in `.aah/codebase-intel/codebase-learning.md §7`). Covers: (a) capability validation — `CapabilityError` is raised when a tool name is absent from `CAPABILITY_MAP` or its declared capabilities do not cover the requested operation; (b) successful file dispatch — `read_file` returns file contents and `write_file` writes content and returns a success string; (c) `run_command` blocklist enforcement — blocked keywords at `agentic_app.py:172` (`"rm "`, `"del "`, `"format "`, `"mkfs"`, `"sudo"`, `"shutdown"`, `":(){"`) produce a `"BLOCKED:"` return without spawning a subprocess, and a safe command (e.g. `"echo hello"`) returns its stdout.

**`tests/test_run_tool.py`** — unit tests for `_run_tool()` in `agentic_tester.py` (lines 150–240). Uses the async mock Playwright page from `tests/conftest.py` (MOD-000). Covers: (a) capability validation — `CapabilityError` is raised when a tool call exceeds its declared capability envelope; (b) `open_page` dispatches to `_page.goto` and returns a JSON payload with `title`, `buttons`, `input_count`, `form_count`; (c) `record_result` appends to the module-global `_results` list and returns a success string.

**`tests/test_iteration_cap.py`** — single regression assertion: imports `agentic_tester` and asserts `agentic_tester.MAX_ITERATIONS == 20`, guarding the guard added in MOD-001 against accidental removal.

**`tests/test_golden.py`** — parametrized pytest test that reads `tests/golden/run_command_golden.yaml` at collection time, iterates over every entry, and asserts the actual blocklist decision for each `command` matches its `expected_outcome` (`allow` or `block`). No subprocess is spawned; the test exercises only the keyword-matching logic extracted from `execute_tool` → `run_command` at `agentic_app.py:172`.

**`tests/golden/run_command_golden.yaml`** — a YAML list of evaluation cases. Each entry is a mapping with `command` (string), `expected_outcome` (one of `allow` or `block`), and `rationale` (string). The set must include at minimum: benign commands that the blocklist allows (`echo`, `python --version`, `ls`, `git status`, `cat README.md`) and adversarial commands that it blocks (`rm -rf /`, `sudo apt-get install`, `del /f /s /q`, `shutdown -r`, `mkfs.ext4`, the fork-bomb prefix `:(){ :|:& };:`). The YAML is read-only at test time and is never written by either agent (see `data-model.md` §Key Data Structures — Golden set entry).

The full capability-validation and flow mechanics are specified in `architecture-overview.md` (Security Controls layer), `application-flow.md` (Blocked path variant), and `data-model.md` (CAPABILITY_MAP and CapabilityError structures). The `codebase-intel/codebase-learning.md §9` confirms there are zero existing test files; all five artefacts are new.

**Behavioral expectations** (the acceptance intent — the build-phase implementer writes TDD tests from these; there is no separate Test Cases section):

- Given `execute_tool` with `CAPABILITY_MAP` populated by MOD-001, when a tool name maps to a capability envelope that does not include the requested operation, then `CapabilityError` is raised and its message is returned as the tool_result string without reaching the tool implementation.
- Given `execute_tool` with a readable file at a known temporary path, when `execute_tool("read_file", {"path": <relative-path>})` is called, then the file's UTF-8 contents are returned as a string.
- Given `execute_tool` with `write_file` capability in scope, when `execute_tool("write_file", {"path": <relative-path>, "content": "hello"})` is called, then the content is written to disk and a non-error string is returned.
- Given `execute_tool`'s `run_command` with a command containing any of the seven blocked keywords at `agentic_app.py:172` (`"rm "`, `"del "`, `"format "`, `"mkfs"`, `"sudo"`, `"shutdown"`, `":(){"`), when `execute_tool("run_command", {"command": <command>})` is called, then the return string begins with `"BLOCKED:"` and no subprocess is spawned.
- Given `execute_tool`'s `run_command` with a safe command containing none of the blocked keywords, when called, then `subprocess.run` is invoked and stdout (or `"(no output)"`) is returned.
- Given `_run_tool` with `CAPABILITY_MAP` populated by MOD-001, when a call is made with a tool name whose declared capabilities do not cover the requested operation, then `CapabilityError` is raised and its message is returned without reaching the Playwright page.
- Given `_run_tool` and the async mock Playwright page fixture from `tests/conftest.py`, when `_run_tool("open_page", {"file_path": <path>})` is awaited, then `_page.goto` is awaited with a `file:///` URL and the return value is a JSON string containing `title`, `buttons`, `input_count`, and `form_count` keys.
- Given `_run_tool` and the async mock Playwright page fixture, when `_run_tool("record_result", {"test_id": "T1", "test_name": "example", "passed": True, "expected": "x", "actual": "x"})` is awaited, then the entry is appended to `agentic_tester._results` and a non-error string is returned.
- Given `agentic_tester` imported after MOD-001 adds `MAX_ITERATIONS`, when `agentic_tester.MAX_ITERATIONS` is read, then it equals `20` exactly.
- Given `tests/golden/run_command_golden.yaml` exists as a valid YAML list, when each entry is loaded at pytest collection time by `test_golden.py`, then every entry has the keys `command`, `expected_outcome`, and `rationale`, and `expected_outcome` is one of `allow` or `block`.
- Given the golden YAML parametrized in `test_golden.py`, when the blocklist logic from `agentic_app.py:172` is applied to each `command`, then the computed outcome matches `expected_outcome` for every case with no failures.
- Given the golden YAML, when the full set is loaded, then at least one entry has `expected_outcome: allow` and at least one has `expected_outcome: block`, ensuring the golden set covers both safe and adversarial inputs.
- Given `pytest tests/ -v` is run after MOD-001 is applied, when all five artefacts are present, then the command exits with code 0 and all collected tests pass.
